claims.title: The Dilmun trading culture flourishes
claims.summary: Around the eastern shores of the Arabian Peninsula, the Dilmun culture became a hub linking Mesopotamia with the Indus valley, remembered in Sumerian literature as a land of prosperity and long life.

sources.label: The Arabian Peninsula: A cradle of ancient kingdoms

claims.title: The kingdom of Lihyan rises at Dadan
claims.summary: The Lihyanite kingdom, centered on Dadan in the AlUla region, grew wealthy from the incense trade and tribute, developing its own language, script, and irrigated agriculture.

sources.label: The Arabian Peninsula: A cradle of ancient kingdoms

claims.title: The Nabataeans make Hegra their southern capital
claims.summary: The Nabataean kingdom extended south and developed Hegra (al-Hijr) as a major caravan city, carving monumental rock-cut tombs that survive as the second-largest Nabataean site after Petra.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-100bce-the-nabataeans-make-hegra-their-southern-capital, claim TL:SAU:event:100bce:the-nabataeans-make-hegra-their-southern-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rome annexes the Nabataean kingdom
claims.summary: The Roman Empire absorbed the Nabataean realm, after which Hegra and the northern caravan cities gradually declined as trade routes shifted.

sources.label: The Arabian Peninsula: A cradle of ancient kingdoms

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-106-rome-annexes-the-nabataean-kingdom, claim TL:SAU:event:106:rome-annexes-the-nabataean-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Birth of Muhammad in Mecca
claims.summary: Muhammad was born in Mecca into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh, the tribe that controlled the pilgrimage sanctuary of the Kaaba.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-570-birth-of-muhammad-in-mecca, claim TL:SAU:event:570:birth-of-muhammad-in-mecca, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The first revelations
claims.summary: According to Islamic tradition Muhammad, at about forty, began receiving revelations through the angel Gabriel, proclaiming a strict monotheism that would form the Quran.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-610-the-first-revelations, claim TL:SAU:event:610:the-first-revelations, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Hijra to Medina
claims.summary: Facing persecution, Muhammad and his followers migrated from Mecca to Yathrib (Medina), founding the first Muslim community; the event marks year one of the Islamic calendar.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-622-the-hijra-to-medina, claim TL:SAU:event:622:the-hijra-to-medina, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The submission of Mecca
claims.summary: Muhammad returned to Mecca largely without bloodshed, cleansed the Kaaba of idols, and established Islam across much of the Hejaz.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-630-the-submission-of-mecca, claim TL:SAU:event:630:the-submission-of-mecca, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Muhammad
claims.summary: By the Prophet's death much of the Arabian Peninsula had embraced Islam, leaving Mecca and Medina as the enduring holy cities of the faith.

claims.title: Medina as capital of the early caliphate
claims.summary: Under the first (Rashidun) caliphs, Medina served as the capital of an expanding Muslim empire before power shifted away from Arabia.

sources.label: Saudi Arabia: A Country Study
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Umayyad and Abbasid rule over the Hejaz
claims.summary: The Umayyads shifted the empire's capital to Damascus and the Abbasids later ruled from Baghdad, leaving Arabia politically peripheral while Mecca and Medina remained its religious centre.

sources.label: Saudi Arabia: A Country Study
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: The Sharifate of Mecca takes shape
claims.summary: A line of sharifs descended from the Prophet came to administer Mecca and the Hejaz, holding local authority for nearly a thousand years under shifting overlords.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-968-the-sharifate-of-mecca-takes-shape, claim TL:SAU:event:968:the-sharifate-of-mecca-takes-shape, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman suzerainty over the Hejaz
claims.summary: After defeating the Mamluks, the Ottomans gained sovereignty over the holy cities; the Sharif of Mecca recognized the Ottoman sultan as caliph while retaining local power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-1517-ottoman-suzerainty-over-the-hejaz, claim TL:SAU:event:1517:ottoman-suzerainty-over-the-hejaz, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Diriyah pact founds the First Saudi State
claims.summary: Muhammad ibn Saud, ruler of Diriyah, and the reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab formed an alliance joining political power and religious revival, the foundation of the first Saudi state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-1744-the-diriyah-pact-founds-the-first-saudi-state, claim TL:SAU:event:1744:the-diriyah-pact-founds-the-first-saudi-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ottoman-Egyptian campaign against the Saudis
claims.summary: On behalf of the Ottoman sultan, the Egyptian forces of Muhammad Ali Pasha waged war on the expanding First Saudi State, driving it from the holy cities and into the Najdi heartland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-1811-the-ottoman-egyptian-campaign-against-the-saudis, claim TL:SAU:event:1811:the-ottoman-egyptian-campaign-against-the-saudis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The fall and destruction of Diriyah
claims.summary: After a months-long siege Ibrahim Pasha took Diriyah in September 1818 and razed it, ending the First Saudi State; the last imam was executed in Constantinople.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-1818-the-fall-and-destruction-of-diriyah, claim TL:SAU:event:1818:the-fall-and-destruction-of-diriyah, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Turki ibn Abdullah founds the Second Saudi State
claims.summary: Turki ibn Abdullah Al Saud expelled the occupying garrisons, re-established Saudi rule, and made Riyadh the capital of a revived but smaller state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-1824-turki-ibn-abdullah-founds-the-second-saudi-state, claim TL:SAU:event:1824:turki-ibn-abdullah-founds-the-second-saudi-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Al Rashid end the Second Saudi State
claims.summary: Weakened by internal feuds, the second state fell to the rival Al Rashid of Hail, who drove the Al Saud into exile in Kuwait.

claims.title: Abdulaziz captures Riyadh
claims.summary: Returning from exile, Abdulaziz ibn Saud and a small force seized the Masmak fortress in Riyadh from the Al Rashid, launching the campaign to rebuild the Saudi state.

sources.label: Ibn Saud: Biography, History, Children, and Facts

claims.title: Conquest of the Hejaz and the holy cities
claims.summary: Abdulaziz's forces took Mecca and Medina, ending Hashemite rule in the Hejaz and bringing the holy cities under Saudi control.

claims.title: The Treaty of Jeddah
claims.summary: Britain formally recognized the independence and sovereignty of Ibn Saud's Kingdom of the Hejaz and Nejd, securing its international standing.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-1927-the-treaty-of-jeddah, claim TL:SAU:event:1927:the-treaty-of-jeddah, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Proclamation of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
claims.summary: By royal decree the regions of Najd and the Hejaz were unified and renamed the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, with Abdulaziz ibn Saud as its first king.

claims.title: The oil concession is granted
claims.summary: Abdulaziz granted an oil exploration concession to the Standard Oil Company of California, the agreement that would become the basis of Aramco.

claims.title: Oil struck at Dammam Well No. 7
claims.summary: Commercial quantities of oil were discovered at Dammam Well No. 7 in March 1938, the find that transformed Saudi Arabia's economy and the world energy market.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-1938-oil-struck-at-dammam-well-no-7, claim TL:SAU:event:1938:oil-struck-at-dammam-well-no-7, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Arab oil embargo
claims.summary: Under King Faisal, Saudi Arabia led Arab OPEC states in an embargo against supporters of Israel, sharply raising oil prices and demonstrating the kingdom's economic power.

claims.title: Hegra becomes a UNESCO World Heritage Site
claims.summary: The Nabataean site of Hegra (al-Hijr) was inscribed as Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognizing the kingdom's deep pre-Islamic past.

claims.title: Vision 2030 is launched
claims.summary: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman unveiled Vision 2030, a program to diversify the economy beyond oil, grow the private sector and tourism, and reshape Saudi society.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Saudi Arabia: From the incense roads of ancient Arabia and the cradle of Islam to the oil-fueled kingdom of the Al Saud.", terralore.co/country/SAU/chronicle#ev-2016-vision-2030-is-launched, claim TL:SAU:event:2016:vision-2030-is-launched, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
